language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hi, I’m Sig. I’m so glad you are able to travel with me in my fishing boat as we explore the Arctic coast of Iceland.
From our boat we can see many types of matter. Matter is anything that has mass and volume. Mass is the measure of how much material makes up an object.

Volume is the amount of space an object takes up. Some objects have more volume than others. For example, a whale takes up more space than a shrimp. So we would say the whale has more volume than a shrimp.

Everything that has mass and volume is matter. They take up space and have mass. Things like sunlight, radio waves, shadows, rainbows, temperature, gravity and time do not have mass or take up space, so they are called ‘non-matter.’
Well, let’s take-off the dock and see what we can find.

When we pull up our fishing net, we find all sorts of interesting types of matter. By using this tank of water, we can measure the volume of an irregularly shaped object.

The volume of the water measures 100 liters. If we put an object in the water, the volume of the water rises. If we subtract the starting point of the water, which is 100 liters, we know the volume of the object.

Our world is full of matter. Matter is defined as anything that has mass and takes up space. If something does not have mass and does not take up space, then it is considered non-matter.
Some examples of non-matter would be rays of sunshine or sound waves from a radio. Can you decide if these objects are considered matter or non-matter?
